v.title: Infantino’s Jet‑Set Scandal: A Barcelona‑Centric Lens
v.excerpt: Infantino’s jet‑set tour sparks a governance debate that could ripple through Barcelona’s future deals and season strategy.
v.body:
## Quick take
Infantino’s 115‑day, 39‑flight private‑jet tour just got exposed, raising questions about FIFA’s governance and its ripple effects on clubs like Barcelona.

## What happened
FIFA president Gianni Infantino embarked on a whirlwind private‑jet campaign across 15 countries over 115 days, reportedly to secure a stake sale in the World Cup’s commercial rights. The BBC uncovered the itinerary, detailing flights, meetings and the high‑profile locations visited. Critics argue the trip’s timing and opacity clash with FIFA’s own transparency pledges.

The revelation comes amid growing scrutiny of FIFA’s executive decisions, especially after the 2026 World Cup hosting bid. Infantino’s move is seen as a strategic play to cement financial control, but it has drawn backlash from national associations and fans alike. The fallout could pressure FIFA to overhaul its procurement and travel policies.

## Why it matters
- **Barcelona’s brand integrity**: The club prides itself on transparency and fair play. Infantino’s jet‑set raises concerns about the governance standards that influence global football economics, potentially affecting club‑level partnerships and sponsorships.
- **Player welfare and contracts**: If FIFA’s commercial deals shift, clubs may face altered revenue streams, impacting salary structures and transfer budgets. Barcelona’s star‑player negotiations could be indirectly affected by the broader financial climate.
- **Seasonal strategy and focus**: With La Liga and Champions League pressures mounting, any instability at FIFA’s top can divert attention and resources. Barcelona’s management may need to brace for potential shifts in tournament scheduling or broadcasting rights.

## What's next
Watch FIFA’s upcoming Congress in March, where Infantino will defend his travel and the World Cup stake sale. Any censure or policy change could force Barcelona to reassess its commercial strategy and engagement with governing bodies. Keep an eye on the club’s official statements and any shifts in partnership deals that might signal a broader recalibration of the football ecosystem.

*Source: [115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cmkgk22w3vlvo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
